# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 13
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 13

---

*[Thomas's farewell address. The martyrdom. Burial.]*

1. The king took counsel with Charisius and Misdaeus and they resolved to put Thomas to death. They feared the people, however, for many loved him.

2. So they took him out of the city in secret, with four soldiers and the officer Charisius, led him to a mountain, and killed him there.

3. But before they led him out, Thomas called the believers to him and addressed them:

4. "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ whom I have preached to you. Love one another as he loved you. Do not be deceived by the troubles of this world, for the troubles of this world are as nothing compared to the rest that has been promised to you.

5. Remember the poor and minister to them, for this is the work of Christ. Do not fear suffering, for the sufferings of this brief time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is to be revealed.

6. And above all, guard the seal you have received and keep holy what is holy, for without it you cannot enter the kingdom."

7. After this he went with them willingly, and they brought him to the mountain.

8. Thomas said to the soldiers: "The will of my Lord be done."

9. He prayed: "My Lord and my God, you know all things. You know my suffering and my labor. You know that I have done your will all my days. Now receive me."

10. He said to Charisius and the soldiers: "Do not look upon me with hatred. I die willingly."

11. The four soldiers pierced him, and he fell.

12. Those who were present wept over him and made great lamentation.

13. Mygdonia and Tertia were there, weeping greatly.

14. Thomas was dead.

15. They wrapped him in fine linen and laid him in an ancient tomb, one in which the kings of old had been buried.

16. Siphor and Gad remained beside his body until the burial was complete.

---
*LOGOS note: Thomas's farewell address (vv.4–6) contains three theological imperatives: believe and love; remember the poor; guard the seal. These are the condensed ethical legacy of the entire ATH. "The will of my Lord be done" (v.8) is the Gethsemane echo. The spear-piercing echoes John 19:34.*
